summary: Thymosin alpha-1 is a peptide in the immunomodulators & host defense class (thymic peptide; TLR-mediated immunomodulation). Europe PMC indexes 1,079 publications naming it or a listed alias in a title or abstract, including 65 randomized controlled trials and 61 clinical trials of any design, as of 2026-09-14. The strongest evidence tier in that literature is human clinical trials. This page reports what those studies state, sentence by sentence, with each statement tied to its source and labeled by the kind of evidence it is. It does not recommend use, and it does not translate study doses into anything personal.

faq.question: Has Thymosin alpha-1 been tested in humans?
faq.answer: Yes. Europe PMC indexes 61 clinical trials and 65 randomized controlled trials naming Thymosin alpha-1 or a listed alias in the title or abstract. The evidence table above lists the ones in this record's ledger with their design and sample size; check the study name, since an alias can refer to a different formulation of the same molecule.

faq.question: What kind of evidence exists for Thymosin alpha-1?
faq.answer: The strongest tier is human clinical trial: human clinical trials. Every claim on this page carries its own tier, because a compound with one human trial and forty animal studies is described by both facts, not the better one.

faq.question: Is Thymosin alpha-1 an approved medicine?
faq.answer: ChEMBL records CHEMBL2103979 at maximum clinical phase 3, with no approval recorded. Approval status differs by jurisdiction and is pending human review on this record.

faq.question: Which species has Thymosin alpha-1 been studied in?
faq.answer: Studies in this record's ledger report work in: Humans, Mice. Findings in one species do not transfer to another, and weight-normalized doses in particular do not scale linearly between them.
